incidents.title: FLASH FLOOD WARNING — Travis County (ACTIVE until ~0600 CDT)
incidents.location: Travis County / Austin Metro — Including Downtown Corridor
incidents.detail: NWS Austin/San Antonio has issued a Flash Flood Warning for Travis County active through approximately 0600 CDT Monday. Heavy thunderstorms are producing 2–3+ inch/hour rainfall rates. Between 1–2 inches have already fallen; additional 1–3 inches possible before warning expires. Flash flooding of creeks, streams, urban areas, highways, streets, and underpasses is occurring or imminent. The Flood Watch follows, extending through Tuesday 7 PM CDT. Life-threatening flooding is possible in low-lying areas. Shoal Creek (west of property) and Waller Creek (east) are at risk of rapid rise. San Jacinto Blvd and Cesar Chavez may see street flooding. Restrict valet and delivery vehicle access on flood-prone approaches. Do NOT send valet drivers to retrieve vehicles during active warning without confirming road conditions. Monitor NWS Austin at weather.gov/ewx for warning updates in real time.

incidents.title: U.S.–Iran MOU ANNOUNCED — Ceasefire Effective; Formal Signing June 19
incidents.detail: President Trump announced Sunday evening: 'The Deal with the Islamic Republic of Iran is now complete.' Iran's Supreme National Security Council confirmed the MOU text was finalized after 15 hours of Qatar-mediated talks. Key terms: immediate and permanent cessation of military operations on all fronts including Lebanon; U.S. naval blockade lifted immediately; Strait of Hormuz to reopen toll-free (formal implementation Friday after signing). Formal signing: June 19, Switzerland. 60-day negotiation window on nuclear program, sanctions, and final agreement begins after signing. Oil prices fell 4.5%+ (Brent ~$83/bbl). AUSTIN RELEVANCE: Iranian cyber retaliation risk SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCED but not eliminated until Strait formally reopens Friday. Maintain elevated cyber posture through June 19. Iranian diaspora response in Austin/UT corridor may include celebratory or mixed gatherings — monitor for spontaneous demonstrations. Brief guest-facing staff: WC-themed phishing still active regardless of deal status — zero-click, zero-QR posture maintained.

incidents.title: FIFA WC Day 5 — Iran vs. New Zealand (SoFi Stadium, LA; midnight CDT)
incidents.location: SoFi Stadium, Inglewood CA / Austin watch parties citywide
incidents.detail: Iran's Group G World Cup opener vs. New Zealand kicks off at 9 PM PT / midnight CDT at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood. Up to 40–50,000 Iranian diaspora protesters expected outside stadium — largest protest of the WC tournament. Pre-revolution lion-and-sun flags banned inside stadium; lawsuit filed by Iranian American Institute. Iranian Sports Minister threatened team would halt match if unofficial flags appear. LA area under heavy security. Iran national team arrived LA Sunday escorted by police; protesters at hotel. MOU announcement Sunday evening may reduce some protest intensity but diaspora grievances around Jan 2026 crackdown remain. Austin watch parties (sports bars, Iranian community venues) expected to be elevated late evening tonight. Monday afternoon also features: Spain vs. Cape Verde (Atlanta, noon CDT), Belgium vs. Egypt (Seattle, 6 PM CDT), Saudi Arabia vs. Uruguay (Miami, 8 PM CDT). WC cyber threat: 10,000+ malicious domains still active; Chinese PRC MitM phishing kit operational — zero-click, zero-QR posture for ALL guest-facing staff.

incidents.title: Paramount Theatre 'Last Call' Open House — 713 Congress Ave (0.5 mi N)
incidents.location: Paramount Theatre, 713 Congress Ave, Austin TX (0.5 mi N)
incidents.detail: The Paramount Theatre (713 Congress Ave, 0.5 mi N) hosts its final public event before closing for an 11-month major restoration. 'Last Call' open house runs 4–8 PM Monday — free with RSVP, tickets reported SOLD OUT. Event unveils the original 1915 hand-painted fire curtain. Expect elevated foot traffic on Congress Ave north of hotel 3–9 PM. Parking demand high — $6 garage at 600 Congress (155 W 7th St entrance). Event is emotionally significant to Austin arts community; generally peaceful, professional crowd. No elevated security concern beyond routine foot traffic and parking congestion. Notify valet and concierge of Congress Ave congestion window 3–9 PM.

incidents.title: APD Tasing Death — Josh Ryan Trumble — DA Investigation Ongoing
incidents.detail: Travis County DA criminal investigation into the June 6 in-custody death of Josh Ryan Trumble, 32, continues. Body cam footage was released publicly Saturday June 14. Seven APD officers remain on administrative leave. APD Chief Lisa Davis has stated department will cooperate fully. Combined No Kings protest activity was generally peaceful Sunday — no reports of major confrontations at Austin Capitol. DA and APD next briefing TBD. Monitor local activist channels for renewed calls for protests or community hearings. LOW watch — no imminent action planned.

incidents.title: Juneteenth Week — Austin Community Events (June 15–19)
incidents.detail: Austin's Juneteenth observance week begins Monday June 15, building toward June 19 (Juneteenth federal holiday). Events include Rosewood Park festivities, community gatherings in East Austin, and cultural programming citywide. Nationally observed holiday brings elevated community visibility, family events, and possible street closures near East Austin venues June 17–19. Guest and staff awareness: hotel may see requests for Juneteenth event recommendations. Generally peaceful, celebratory. No security elevation required for Monday; monitor as week progresses toward June 19.
